h1: The 5 Best 60V Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 genuine Greenworks 60V cordless leaf blowers scored on airflow, kit contents and turbo, from 450 CFM to 700 CFM brushless.
summary: The Greenworks 700 CFM brushless blower is the most powerful genuine 60V model here and the best overall for large, tree-heavy yards. The 2.5Ah kit is the right start for anyone without a 60V battery, delivering 610 CFM and about 50 minutes of listed runtime. The two Pro bare tools suit existing owners, and the 450 CFM model is strictly for patios and light debris.
intro: Greenworks lists its 60V blowers in two forms that look the same in search results: complete kits with a battery and charger, and bare tools with an empty box. Buying the wrong one is the classic mistake here. A bare tool is a bargain if you own 60V packs and an expensive paperweight if you do not, and the price gap between the two tells you nothing about the blowers themselves.

This ranking keeps only genuine 60V blowers, orders them by airflow, and then adjusts for what ships in the box. Our editors reviewed spec sheets and owner feedback for five models, scored them on the Primea framework, and flagged every bare tool. Compare kits with kits and bare tools with bare tools, never across.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 700 CFM Brushless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 700 CFM with a variable speed dial and turbo button. The strongest genuine 60V model here.
products.description:
The 700 CFM Greenworks is the top of the genuine 60V range, and the extra airflow is the reason to buy it. Moving a pile of damp leaves is a volume problem, not a speed problem, so a high CFM figure clears a yard in fewer passes. A brushless motor drives it, a dial sets the speed, and a turbo button adds a burst when a stubborn patch sticks.

It ranks above the 610 CFM kit by about 90 CFM and a lighter, more comfortable grip, but it costs more, in the $200 to $500 bucket. Fewer owners have used it than the older models.

Choose it for a big lot with heavy leaf drop. The caveat is the box: confirm in the listing whether a battery is included before you pay the premium.
products.idealFor: Large yards with heavy leaf drop.
products.skipIf: You have a small yard or only light debris.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Electric Leaf Blower with 2.5Ah Battery
products.verdict: 610 CFM, 50 minutes on the included 2.5Ah battery, turbo up to 130 MPH.
products.description:
This is the kit to buy if you own no Greenworks 60V gear. The 610 CFM blower arrives with a 2.5Ah battery that the listing rates at about 50 minutes of runtime, and turbo raises air speed to as much as 130 MPH for glued-down debris. One box gives you a working tool, which the bare-tool rivals cannot say.

It sits second because it moves 90 CFM less than the 700 and costs more than the bare 610 CFM Pro. If you already own a pack, you are paying for a battery you do not need.

Pick it for a first-time 60V buyer with an average yard. The caveat: 2.5Ah is a modest pack, and turbo drains it quicker than the 50 minute figure implies, so a second battery is wise for large lots.

products.name: Greenworks Pro Bare Tool 60V 610 CFM GEN2 Blower
products.verdict: 610 CFM with turbo and a concentrator nozzle, sold without battery or charger.
products.description:
The GEN2 Pro bare tool matches the kit's 610 CFM and adds a concentrator nozzle, which narrows the airstream so it lifts wet leaves and caked debris off a lawn. Turbo helps in the same way. Pairing that airflow with a battery you already own is the cheapest route to a strong blower in this ranking.

It ranks third because the box holds no battery or charger. Against the kit above, the saving only exists if you own the pack, and a newcomer ends up paying more once a battery is added. It also edges the 540 CFM Pro with 70 more CFM for a small step up in cost.

Buy it if 60V packs already fill a shelf in your garage. Skip it otherwise, because without a battery it does nothing.
pros: Saves money with your own pack
products.idealFor: Greenworks owners who already have 60V batteries.

products.name: Greenworks Pro Bare Tool 60V 540 CFM Blower
products.verdict: The lowest price here, with a brushless motor and cruise control, as a bare tool.
products.description:
The 540 CFM Pro is the cheapest way into brushless power on this platform. A brushless motor means less wear and quieter running, and the variable trigger with cruise control lets you lock a speed during long passes along a fence line or driveway. For a small yard that is plenty of control.

It trails the 610 CFM bare tool because that model offers 70 more CFM for a modest step up in cost, so unless the budget is the hard limit, the stronger one is the better buy. Like it, this unit ships without battery or charger.

Choose it if you have 60V packs and a modest yard with light leaf cover. The caveat is airflow: at 540 CFM, thick wet drifts will take many more passes.
products.idealFor: 60V owners on a tight budget with a smaller yard.
products.skipIf: You need a battery in the box.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Electric Leaf Blower (450 CFM)
products.verdict: The lowest airflow here at 450 CFM, with adjustable wind power for varied tasks.
products.description:
The 450 CFM blower is a sweeping tool, not a leaf-clearing one. Adjustable wind power lets you dial down for patios and driveways, where you want to move grit and dry leaves, not shove a wet pile across a lawn. It is the lightest-duty model here and the one you hold longest without fatigue.

It lands last because airflow is the whole purpose of a leaf blower, and the 540 and 610 CFM models both outpush it. Wet, packed leaves are where it runs out of volume. It also shares the check-the-box risk, since a listing may not include a pack.

Buy it for a small yard with hard surfaces and dry debris. Skip it if you clear an autumn's worth of heavy, damp leaves.

whatMatters.detail: A bare tool ships without a battery or charger, so it only works if you already own a compatible 60V Greenworks pack. A kit includes both and works from the box. The price difference between them is not a performance difference. Read the title for the words bare tool or with battery, then check the box contents list before ordering.

CFM measures how much air moves, which clears piles, while MPH measures how fast it hits, which loosens stuck debris. For leaves, volume does more work, so rank by CFM first. Between 540 and 700 CFM covers most yards, and under 500 is light work. Look for the CFM figure in the title or specifications, not just MPH.

Amp-hours measure how much energy a battery stores, so a bigger number means more minutes between charges. The 2.5Ah kit battery is listed at about 50 minutes at normal speed, and turbo drains it faster. For a large property, a second pack removes the mid-job wait. Check the amp-hour rating on any battery shown with a tool.

Brushless motors drop the carbon brushes that wear out in cheaper designs, so they run quieter, cooler and last longer. The benefit is most obvious on a tool used often. The 700 CFM and 540 CFM models list a brushless motor. Look for the word brushless in the specifications rather than assuming it from the price.

You hold a blower at arm's length, so balance and grip determine how long you can work before fatigue. A lightweight body with a comfortable handle cuts strain, and the battery adds to the carried load. Compare listed weights, remember the pack is extra on bare tools, and favour designs with a trigger that lets you lock speed.

faq.q: Do I need to buy a battery separately?
faq.a: For the two Pro bare tools, yes. The 610 CFM GEN2 and the 540 CFM Pro ship without a battery or charger. The 2.5Ah Greenworks kit includes one, so it is the safer route if you own no 60V packs.
They are separate platforms, not better or worse on voltage alone. Choose by the batteries you already own and the tool range you want. A 60V Greenworks blower will not use a 56V pack.
Between 540 and 700 CFM clears most yards. The 700 CFM model suits big, tree-heavy lots, while the 450 CFM unit is only sensible for patios, driveways and dry debris on small lawns.

It means the motor has no carbon brushes, so it runs quieter, cooler and wears more slowly. The 700 CFM and 540 CFM Greenworks models list brushless motors. Check the specifications for the word itself.

faq.q: How long will the 2.5Ah battery last?
faq.a: The listing says about 50 minutes at normal speed. Turbo drains the pack faster, so expect less if you lean on it. For a large yard, buy a second battery instead of stretching one charge.

faq.q: Can I use an EGO battery on a Greenworks blower?
faq.a: No. Batteries are specific to each brand and platform, so an EGO pack will not fit a Greenworks 60V blower. Match the pack to the tool, or buy the 2.5Ah kit so the pieces are already compatible.

finalTake: Buy the 700 CFM model if you own or will buy 60V batteries and have a lot of leaves to move. Buy the 2.5Ah kit if the battery is the missing piece. Pick the 610 CFM bare tool only if a pack is already in your garage, and leave the 450 CFM unit for hard surfaces and small lawns.
